The A18 harness (QA_A18_REQUIRE=1) passed 10/10 ('matched'). The harness's own S2-S8 re-check, extracted verbatim from the frozen file, accepts the live run3/b entry and rejects 8 tampered copies. (2) Trying to make the rule explain what it must not. On the kept, disposable run3/b target, using the shipped CLI unchanged, one committed mutation at a time: an initiating user; an event trigger with a schedule-format key; the schedule row disabled; the key on a real slot 15 min before the window; a key two minutes after the slot; created_at before W0; a second execution for the same slot that the recheck did not list; the execution's worker event re-attributed to a user; and the execution id in the package (a changed row). Each gives exit 1 with the exact A5.4 reason. An extra unrelated table (approval_request changed) and an 'unexplained changed' key each make Gate 0 not applicable. Restored, the target passes again, and the job_schedule and pgboss.schedule digests are unchanged throughout (the stage is read only). Pure-function probes: 45 cases incl. exact boundaries (slot = W1 inside, W1 + 1 ms outside, W0 - 60 s outside, W0 - 59.999 s inside, daily cron in the row's zone vs UTC, 20 keys truncated, 19 keys with 18 unknown), all as expected. Mutation check: 12 single-condition mutants of the rule (S1-S9, uniqueness, Gate 0 table and key-line checks, S6 widened to 2 min, S7 widened to 120 s) are all killed by DO-D9's own T-S1..T-S8. The deploy-script suite passes 204/204, including T-S9 on PostgreSQL. (3) Soundness: the rule is exactly D-278. Mode 2 itself is unchanged and stays as strict as before; only the drill's second stage reads it, and it reads only automation rows. The documented recovery (re-run the drill, never pause a schedule) is correct. The remaining residuals (a handler's own business writes, engine ticks, pg-boss timing) fail strict, never loose. Disclosure: deployment.md and the register notes carry the rule. known-limitations.md and the release notes do not, against ADR-0064 A5.6. That is raised separately as F-DG7-972 (Low) and does not reopen F-DG7-971, whose expected result accepted the decision plus a drill change, or a disclosure with the recovery.
